title: Phenomenology, existentialism and process philosophy
audience: a college student in a philosophy degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Study the continental and process traditions on being and experience: Brentano and Husserl on intentionality and the phenomenological method, Heidegger's question of being and being-in-the-world, Sartre and de Beauvoir on freedom and existence, Merleau-Ponty on the body and perception, Bergson on duration, and Whitehead's process metaphysics.

weeks.2: Husserl: the phenomenological method and the epoché
weeks.8: De Beauvoir: the ethics of ambiguity and The Second Sex
weeks.12: Process thought, analytic metaphysics and the dialogue between traditions

blocks.deliverable: Describe an experience using the phenomenological method.
Week 7 midterm; explain Sartre's claim that existence precedes essence.
Compare Bergson's duration with clock time.
Write a three-page comparison of process and substance views.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Comparative paper: write a 2,500-word paper comparing how a phenomenological, existentialist or process philosopher and an analytic metaphysician answer the same question (what time is, what a self is, or what it is to exist), and assess what each approach captures that the other misses.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
